# Privacy Preserving Systems Lab (PPS Lab)

> The Privacy Preserving Systems Lab (PPS Lab) is a research group led by Anwar Hithnawi at the University of Toronto. We build, investigate, and research software systems for data privacy and data security. Research areas: Secure and Robust Collaborative Learning; End-to-End Designs for Data Privacy; Accessible Privacy Preserving Computation; Privacy Preserving Stream Analytics at Scale.

Our mission is to develop technologies that enable applications to safely and securely interact with users' data while preserving individuals' privacy, and to make it easy for developers to build privacy-preserving applications. The lab was founded at ETH Zurich and is now at the University of Toronto.

Website: https://pps-lab.com/. The full text of this site is at https://pps-lab.com/llms-full.txt. Machine-readable publication lists: https://pps-lab.com/publications.json and https://pps-lab.com/publications.bib.

## Research areas

- [Secure and Robust Collaborative Learning](https://pps-lab.com/research/ml-sec/): Machine learning algorithms continue to achieve remarkable success in a wide range of applications.
- [End-to-End Designs for Data Privacy](https://pps-lab.com/research/e2e-privacy/): As increasing quantities of sensitive data are collected to gain valuable insights, the need to natively integrate privacy controls in data frameworks is growing in importance.
- [Accessible Privacy Preserving Computation](https://pps-lab.com/research/fhe/): Privacy and security are gaining tremendous importance across all organizations as public perception of these issues has shifted and expectations, including regulatory demands, have increased.
- [Privacy Preserving Stream Analytics at Scale](https://pps-lab.com/research/pp-stream/): Recent years have seen unprecedented growth in networked devices and services that continuously collect increasingly detailed information about individuals.

## Publications

- [Scaling Zero Knowledge UNSAT Verification via Normalized Chaining](https://pps-lab.com/publications/scaling-zkunsat/): Ashwin Karthikeyan, Ethan Kharitonov, Kuldeep S. Meel, Anwar Hithnawi. Conference on Logic for Programming, Artificial Intelligence, and Reasoning (LPAR 2026), 2026. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19353. Code: https://github.com/meelgroup/chain-normalize.git.

- [Towards Practical Zero-Knowledge Proof for PSPACE](https://pps-lab.com/publications/zkpspace/): Ashwin Karthikeyan, Hengyu Liu, Kuldeep S. Meel, Ning Luo. IEEE Security and Privacy (Oakland) 2026, 2026. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.15071. Code: https://github.com/PP-FM/zkqbf-suite.

IEEE Security and Privacy (Oakland) 2025, 2025. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06747. Code: https://github.com/pps-lab/dpolicy. Slides: https://pps-lab.com/files/DPolicy_SP25_presentation.pdf.

## Blog

- [Verifying Apple Reference Images](https://pps-lab.com/blog/verifying-apple-reference-image/) (2026-11-02, Hidde Lycklama, Alexander Viand): With the new iPhone 18 Pro series, Apple created a new standard to verify the authenticity of images taken on iPhones, called Apple Reference Image.
- [Secure LLM Inference with MP-SPDZ](https://pps-lab.com/blog/secure-token-prediction-with-bert-in-mp-spdz/) (2026-05-24, Hidde Lycklama): LLMs are now the standard benchmark in encrypted AI research. Producing real next-token predictions using research frameworks, however, remains challenging.
- [Does It Matter How You Pick Your Batches?](https://pps-lab.com/student-blogs/does-it-matter-how-you-pick-your-batches/) (2026-04-13, Andy Cai, Yvonne Yifeng Peng): Shuffle-without-replacement is widely used as a drop-in for Poisson subsampling in DP-SGD — but the two carry very different privacy guarantees, and the gap can reach 10× in the worst case.
- [Private Set Intersection for Training Data Auditing](https://pps-lab.com/student-blogs/private-set-intersection-for-training-data-auditing/) (2026-04-12, Angela Sha, Sierra Wyllie): We use fuzzy private set intersection between an individual's images and a training set to determine if their data was used to train a model.
- [zkPi+](https://pps-lab.com/student-blogs/zkpi-plus/) (2026-04-08, Ethan Bodzioney, Matthew Toohey): zkPi is a tool capable of verifying Lean proofs independently without sharing any information about the inner workings of the proof (zero-knowledge).
- [Lean4FHE](https://pps-lab.com/student-blogs/lean4fhe/) (2026-04-08, Ashwin Karthikeyan, Maite Kramarz): A verified compiler from Boolean circuits to GSW homomorphic encryption circuits, written and proven correct in Lean 4 with Mathlib.
- [A primer on the FHEW & TFHE schemes](https://pps-lab.com/blog/fhew_tfhe/) (2023-10-27, Christian Knabenhans): Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is a cryptographic primitive that allows one to perform computations on encrypted data.
- [Arithmetizing FHE in Circom](https://pps-lab.com/blog/fhe_arithmetization/) (2023-10-27, Christian Knabenhans): Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) allows one to perform computations on encrypted data, making it particularly useful for providing privacy to computations.
